item.title: Drone strikes kill 3: Kyiv hits Omsk plant and Ozon hub; power cut in Crimea and east
item.description: Ukraine launched drone strikes against Russian targets in Omsk, hitting a petrochemical plant and a warehouse. In retaliation, a Russian drone attack on Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region resulted in three civilian deaths and injuries. The strikes also caused significant disruptions to electricity in Crimea and other occupied areas of Ukraine. Power restoration efforts are ongoing as residents face temporary power cuts.
item.dc:creator: Vijaya Srivastava

item.title: Solar storm delayed a train by 16 minutes in 1848, not 1841: How scientists solved a 155-year-old mystery
item.description: A fascinating correction has emerged from the archives concerning a train delay in Exeter. Initially reported incorrectly, researchers have clarified that the incident actually transpired on October 18, 1848. This revelation was achieved through the analysis of railway records and contemporary newspapers, alongside geomagnetic data, which pointed to a significant solar storm influencing the delay during that time.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Dallas homeowners lost their $58,150 repair claim after a court ruled they filed too late
item.description: A federal appeals court has ruled against Dallas residents who sought over $58,000 from State Farm for water damage from a 2021 freeze, determining that their lawsuit was not filed within the required timeframe of their insurance policy. State Farm had already compensated for initial damages but denied further claims, especially since the homeowners declined additional living costs during property repairs.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Alleged Mortgage Fraud Exposed: Lawsuits detail DSCR loan flips; Baltimore housing suffers
item.description: In 2022, a property in Baltimore purchased for $43,000 astonishingly changed hands for $310,000 just a year later. This sharp spike in valuation has led to accusations of inflated property prices by investors, resulting in numerous foreclosures. Federal lawsuits allege a scheme involving over 150 properties generating millions in loans, prompting lender scrutiny and investigations into the housing market, revealing Baltimore's deep-seated issues with housing insecurity.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 170-year-old portrait sold for $882 in 2025 fetches $230,400 after man's identity is discovered
item.description: A photograph that fetched $882 at a New York auction last year has now been identified as a portrait of George Boyer Vashon, the first licensed African American lawyer in New York State. Experts recognized its historical significance, leading Sotheby's to auction it for an astonishing $230,400, far surpassing its initial estimate. This revelation underscores the profound impact of historical context on art valuation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Ohio court upheld Wells Fargo’s $449,905 foreclosure after three loan modifications over 17 years
item.description: In a recent decision, an Ohio appeals court upheld the foreclosure ruling against Sandra Doberdruk, stemming from her unpaid mortgage. Doberdruk's financial troubles escalated after her husband's passing in 2009, despite her attempts to modify her loan thrice. Wells Fargo eventually moved forward with foreclosure after missed payments, and the court ruled that her late husband's estate was not a necessary party in the proceedings.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 9-year-old can write 10 languages and a dozen fonts
item.description: Meet Sebastian Esposito, a 9-year-old prodigy from New Mexico, gifted with the ability to write in an impressive ten languages. Diagnosed with autism, his journey took a remarkable turn when he developed hyperlexia, allowing him to read at an early age. With a knack for memorizing the periodic table and identifying flags by their shapes, Sebastian’s parents showcase his extraordinary talents on social media to foster autism awareness.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: NY court dismissed a foreclosure case after the lender waited three years to seek a default ruling
item.description: In a significant ruling, a New York appeals court has supported the dismissal of a mortgage foreclosure lawsuit against a borrower after the lender delayed three years to seek a default judgment. New York regulations stipulate that lenders must act within one year of a borrower's non-response to avoid case dismissal. This decision reinforces homeowner protections and emphasizes the importance of timely legal actions in foreclosure matters.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Hilda Payin’s 200+ autographs, including Babe Ruth and Amelia Earhart, sell for $28,759 at auction
item.description: A remarkable scrapbook assembled by Hilda Jeanne Payin in the 1930s was auctioned for an impressive $28,759. This unique collection boasts over 200 signatures from iconic figures across sports, politics, and entertainment, including legends like Babe Ruth and Amelia Earhart, as well as presidents Calvin Coolidge and Herbert Hoover. Each item features personal notes linking them closely to Payin, creating a fascinating historical narrative of 20th-century influencers.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2016, a Texas couple took in 2 goats in their tiny South Austin backyard; 10 years later, Austin Farm Sanctuary covers 95 acres
item.description: In 2016, Chris Fuller-Wigg and Angela established the Austin Farm Sanctuary after rescuing a pair of goats, marking the beginning of a transformative journey. Today, the sanctuary spans 95 acres and shelters around 240 animals, many of whom are elderly or disabled. With its innovative LEAP program, visitors engage in hands-on experiences that foster compassion for farm animals, challenging traditional views and promoting a kinder perspective on these sentient beings.

item.title: Helen Mirren, 81, is on a mission to save Italy’s 1,500-year-old olive trees from deadly bacteria
item.description: Helen Mirren, 81, is fighting to save Italy’s ancient olive trees from Xylella fastidiosa, a deadly bacterium that has reportedly destroyed around 22 million trees since 2013. Through her initiative, Save the Olives, the Oscar winner is supporting conservation efforts and developing resistant varieties. “We have to save these trees,” she says.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Sturges House Preservation Dispute: Neglect now threatens Wright landmark; code violations fuel showdown
item.description: The Sturges House, an architectural masterpiece by Frank Lloyd Wright completed in 1939, is facing severe preservation challenges. Preservationists warn of significant neglect and deterioration of this Los Angeles landmark. While the property owner asserts millions spent on upkeep, ongoing concerns linger unresolved. Urgent action is needed as preservation groups and city officials scrutinize the potential loss of the structure's iconic cantilever feature.
